### (Root) Mean Square Error {background="#43464B" visibility="uncounted"}


 
####

Why MSE so often? 


- Explicitly know

#### MSE-Optimal Forecast

<div class="rounded-box">

::: {#prp-pred-mse-opt}

Suppose that $Y$ has finite second moments. Then
$$
\E[Y|\bX] \in \argmin_{f(\cdot): \E[f(\bX)^2]<\infty}  \E[ (Y-f(\bX))^2]
$$

:::


</div>

- MSE-best guess: conditional expectation of $Y$
- Explains in what sense $\E[Y|\bX]$ was the "best guess" for $Y$ given "information" $\bX$

 

#### Proof I: Expansion

Key trick: add and subtract $\E[Y|\bX]$ under the MSE
$$
\begin{aligned}
MSE(f) & = \E[(Y- f(\bX))^2] \\
& = \E\left[\left( (Y-\E[Y|\bX]) + (\E[Y|\bX] - f(\bX)) \right)^2\right]  \\
& = \E\left[  (Y-\E[Y|\bX])^2 \right] + \E[(\E[Y|\bX] - f(\bX))^2]\\
& \quad + 2\E\left[  (Y-\E[Y|\bX]) (\E[Y|\bX] - f(\bX)) \right]
\end{aligned}
$$




#### Proof II: Cross-Term = 0

Recall

<div class="rounded-box">

Law of iterated expectations: for any variables $V, W$ it holds that $\E[V]= \E[ \E[V|W]]$. 

</div>

. . .

It follows that (why?)
$$
\E\left[  (Y-\E[Y|\bX]) (\E[Y|\bX] - f(\bX)) \right] = 0
$$

#### Proof III: Conclusion

So
$$
MSE(f) = \E\left[  (Y-\E[Y|\bX])^2 \right] + \E[(\E[Y|\bX] - f(\bX))^2]
$$

- First term does not depend on $f$
- Second term minimized by taking $f(\bX) = \E[Y|\bX]$

. . . 

Result follows

#### Root MSE

Typically RMSE

- in the same units as the outcome, more interpretable than raw MSE
